entry_point: Media API route handlers of the first-party storage adapters: presigned upload (GET ?key=), direct upload, single and batch delete, copy/move and listing, on the S3, DigitalOcean Spaces, Azure Blob and Cloudinary backends

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned commit: an out-of-root key or directory handed to each adapter's route handler (pages-router req/res for S3/DOS/Cloudinary, app-router Request/NextResponse for Azure and the injected S3 app-router module) reaches the storage SDK unchanged. The SDKs are replaced by in-memory stubs; authorized() returns true.

routes: No pattern-B uncovered route (unmodified upstream code reaching the same sink with the protection missing) was found: at the pinned commit every adapter's write/delete/list path lacks the confinement uniformly. The extra levers are injected siblings (track=injected), registered below.

patch_checks.why: fresh agent, report + repo only (written downstream)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the stated refusal form is a 4xx client error, so a crash or 500 fails the same security tests (they require a client error, not one exact status).
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: every guard decides exactly the object key or directory the route then hands to the storage SDK; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: the media API has no role/direction split; the copy route's source and destination are both asserted in the same test, so a one-side fix fails it.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: upload, delete (single and batch), copy and listing are asserted by separate tests; a read-only guard leaves the write tests failing.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: confinement depends on no external authority secret or role, so there is no result that can be missing and make the guard fail open.

traps.shape: Azure Blob app-router upload/delete/list and Cloudinary multipart upload (folder and filename), delete and list; neither adapter has a media-root option, but absolute, traversal, NUL/backslash and empty values are still refused
traps.reason_to_dismiss: those adapters have no media-root option, so a solver argues there is no boundary to escape and an authenticated editor already owns the container

traps.shape: S3 batch delete: DELETE ?keys=<repeated> resolves every key in the array against the media root, refusing the whole batch when one is invalid
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a fix to the single-asset delete branch never reaches the separate multi-select route and its array input shape
traps.realistic_because: a media manager multi-select action is naturally its own Next API route next to the single-asset one, reusing the same SDK client and DeleteObjects command

traps.shape: S3 app-router media handlers: GET presign and listing, POST direct upload, DELETE route delete; every caller key is resolved against the media root
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported handler is the pages-router one; a parallel app-router export in another module looks like a separate surface
traps.realistic_because: the Azure adapter already ships app-router handlers, so adding the same shape for the object-store adapter is an obvious parity feature, exported from the package index
coupled_functional_tests: functional/injected_routes.test.ts::mints a presigned upload url for a nested key
functional/injected_routes.test.ts::accepts a direct upload for a nested key

traps.shape: DOS copy/move route: POST ?from=&to= resolves the source and destination keys against the media root before CopyObject
traps.reason_to_dismiss: copy is neither upload nor delete, so a fix aimed at the reported operations skips it
traps.realistic_because: a move/rename in the media manager is naturally a copy endpoint; it takes caller-chosen source and destination keys and uses the same SDK client
